lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Personal Planning Systems Under Real Load
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: task breakdown and sequencing

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic task breakdown and sequencing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner selects one real assignment or project currently due within the next three weeks and produces a written, sequenced breakdown of the concrete steps needed to finish it, ordered from first to last with an estimated day for each.
safetyNotes: This task produces a planning document only; it does not require the learner to complete or submit the actual assignment as part of this lesson.
materials: adult-or-local: one real upcoming multi-step assignment or project with a known due date

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific way this sequenced breakdown changes what you will actually do differently this week, compared to how you would have approached this assignment without it.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Concreteness and completeness of the step list: At least five concrete, specific steps are listed that together plausibly cover the assignment from start to submission. | Sequencing and time estimation: Steps are in a logical order with a day or date estimate for each, ending on or before the actual due date. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner apply the same five-step breakdown process to a second real upcoming assignment or project with a different due date, then compare the two sequenced lists to find one planning pattern that shows up in both.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic task breakdown and sequencing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a document

localMaterials.label: one real upcoming multi-step assignment or project with a known due date
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

resources.title: task breakdown and sequencing worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner selects one real assignment or project currently due within the next three weeks and produces a written, sequenced breakdown of the concrete steps needed to finish it, ordered from first to last with an estimated day for each.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact task breakdown and sequencing decision or action.
Model move 2: Name the real assignment or project you will break down and its actual due date.
Model move 3: List every concrete step needed to finish the assignment, from the very first action to turning it in, without worrying yet about order.

Model check: Concreteness and completeness of the step list: At least five concrete, specific steps are listed that together plausibly cover the assignment from start to submission. | Sequencing and time estimation: Steps are in a logical order with a day or date estimate for each, ending on or before the actual due date.

resources.title: task breakdown and sequencing action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for task breakdown and sequencing.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: task breakdown and sequencing coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner selects one real assignment or project currently due within the next three weeks and produces a written, sequenced breakdown of the concrete steps needed to finish it, ordered from first to last with an estimated day for each.
Coach direction: Name the real assignment or project you will break down and its actual due date.
Learner prompt: Name the specific assignment or project and its due date, and describe in one sentence why it counts as multi-step rather than something you could finish in one sitting.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: task breakdown and sequencing complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: List every concrete step needed to finish the assignment, from the very first action to turning it in, without worrying yet about order.

Response 1 (t2-p1): List every concrete step you can think of that this assignment actually requires (examples: 'pick a topic,' 'find three sources,' 'write a rough draft of section two,' not vague steps like 'work on it').
Response 2 (t2-p2): I listed at least five distinct concrete steps, not fewer.
Response 3 (t2-p3): Each step names a specific action, not a vague phrase like 'work on it' or 'get started.'
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: task breakdown and sequencing minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific way this sequenced breakdown changes what you will actually do differently this week, compared to how you would have approached this assignment without it.

Success checks: Concreteness and completeness of the step list: At least five concrete, specific steps are listed that together plausibly cover the assignment from start to submission. | Sequencing and time estimation: Steps are in a logical order with a day or date estimate for each, ending on or before the actual due date.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: task breakdown and sequencing supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional task breakdown and sequencing condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Concreteness and completeness of the step list: At least five concrete, specific steps are listed that together plausibly cover the assignment from start to submission. | Sequencing and time estimation: Steps are in a logical order with a day or date estimate for each, ending on or before the actual due date..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner selects one real assignment or project currently due within the next three weeks and produces a written, sequenced breakdown of the concrete steps needed to finish it, ordered from first to last with an estimated day for each.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Name the specific assignment or project and its due date, and describe in one sentence why it counts as multi-step rather than something you could finish in one sitting.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Concreteness and completeness of the step list: At least five concrete, specific steps are listed that together plausibly cover the assignment from start to submission.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

simulationRoute.title: task breakdown and sequencing — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the task breakdown and sequencing task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain one specific way this sequenced breakdown changes what you will actually do differently this week, compared to how you would have approached this assignment without it.
observableCriteria: Concreteness and completeness of the step list: At least five concrete, specific steps are listed that together plausibly cover the assignment from start to submission.
Sequencing and time estimation: Steps are in a logical order with a day or date estimate for each, ending on or before the actual due date.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Concreteness and completeness of the step list: At least five concrete, specific steps are listed that together plausibly cover the assignment from start to submission. | Sequencing and time estimation: Steps are in a logical order with a day or date estimate for each, ending on or before the actual due date.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
